blocks.source: Vol IV, Closed-Loop Evaluation, § Closed-Loop Dynamics
blocks.md: A policy checkpoint that achieves the lowest validation loss on held-out teleoperation logs can drive the mobile base into a warehouse rack or jam the door latch on its first physical trial. Offline scoring resets the robot's state to the demonstrator's recording at every step, erasing the cumulative consequences of the policy's own actions.

questions.q: The section **Closed-Loop Dynamics** develops one of the chapter's claims. Which one?
options: A finite record supports a claim only if the target ODD, its weights, approximately independent draws, a frozen predicate, and the full denominator are fixed before the first run.

The evaluation record binds a bounded claim to its target ODD, configuration digests, sampling protocol, complete outcome log, exact statistics, and the catalog of unsupported gaps, which become runtime obligations.
Hazards are rates per operating hour, and bounding a rate lambda with zero events needs about 3/lambda failure-free hours, so rare hazards cannot be demonstrated by sampling the proposer.

At zero failures the Wald interval collapses, so a clean record is inverted exactly (failure bound about 3/n), which makes twenty clean runs consistent with a one-in-seven failure rate and makes every added nine cost about ten times the trials.
